sentences.text: Confuciusornis was an avialan theropod dinosaur roughly the size of a modern crow.
This creature measured about 50 cm in length with a wingspan reaching up to 70 cm.
Estimates of its body weight suggest a range from 0.2 kg to 0.5 kg.
It possessed a beak without teeth, a feature similar to those seen in modern birds.
Paleontologists Hou Lianhai and Hu Yoaming discovered the genus in November 1993.
The genus was formally described by Hou and colleagues in 1995.
The type species for this genus is Confuciusornis sanctus.
Four additional species have since been described, including C. dui, C. feducciai, C. jianchangensis, and C. shifan.
Like modern birds, Confuciusornis had a beak that lacked teeth.
The loss of teeth in Confuciusornis likely occurred convergently with that of contemporary birds like Hesperornis and Ichthyornis.
Researchers suggest that mass deaths of Confuciusornis flocks were caused by volcanic eruptions releasing ash, heat, or poisonous gas.
Hou originally assigned Confuciusornis to the family Confuciusornithidae in 1995.
Later, Hou concluded that Confuciusornis was the sister taxon of Enantiornithes within the group Sauriurae.
Currently, only the species Confuciusornis sanctus is universally accepted by scientists.
The genus Jinzhouornis, named by Hou in 2002, is now considered a junior synonym of Confuciusornis.
Fossils of Confuciusornis date to the Early Cretaceous period.
The animal lived between 125 and 120 million years ago.
The Yixian and Jiufotang Formations, where fossils are found, are now dated to the Lower Cretaceous, between 131 and 120 million years ago.
Remains of this dinosaur are found in the Yixian and Jiufotang Formations in China.
It is debated whether paratype specimens definitively belong to the species Confuciusornis sanctus due to a lack of overlapping bones with the holotype.
It is debated whether differences between named species of Confuciusornis represent distinct species or just individual variation within a single species.
Early interpretations exaggerated primitive traits, such as when Hou assumed in 1995 that the animal had a long tail and mistook jaw bone grooves for teeth.

It is debated whether Confuciusornis possesses an ancestral diapsid skull; while it was considered the first known bird with this trait in the late 1990s, a 2018 study concluded the temporal configuration was an autapomorphic trait unique to the group.
